description.narrative: Beyond raising awareness and promoting energy efficiency, the project will back municipal activities aimed at implementing green transition measures. This includes providing energy audits for selected municipal buildings, designing and co-funding infrastructure upgrades to meet established targets. These efforts will enable municipalities to pursue infrastructure upgrades using their own funds, state resources, or contributions from other donors. The scope of energy efficiency audits and technical assistance will encompass not only municipal buildings, but also schools, kindergartens, sports and cultural infrastructure, street/façade and park lighting, irrigation systems, and other municipal responsibilities. Given that non-municipal and residential buildings are the largest energy consumers, the project will extend support for energy efficiency audits of residential buildings in IDPs and eco-migrants compact settlements, residential buildings selected by municipalities for infrastructure upgrades. Energy efficiency upgrades may also include the use of solar energy. In addition to energy efficiency infrastructure upgrades, the project will support development of energy efficiency audit reports, technical recommendations, or design documentation to assist municipalities in mobilizing financing from sources such as MRDI-led ITDP and other state or donor programs.

title.narrative: Number of knowledge and experience sharing, and collaboration activities conducted to support promotion of good practices

description.narrative: Cooperation between the target municipalities will be supported, including through mentoring and peer-to-peer learning applied by the DGG project. The project will facilitate the exchange of knowledge and good practices among municipalities, sharing successful initiatives and services and enabling municipalities to replicate good practices. Cooperation with other Georgian municipalities advanced in green transition through peer-to-peer learning and support of implementation of pilot initiatives will be provided. Among others, this effort will include support NALAG, which is implementing an annual Best Practices Program effectively promoted through the DGG project's support in previous years, with the aim to introduce and develop green and just transition related Best Practices Awards, support and incentivize municipalities to increase quality and scale of green projects, strengthen NALAG capacities to promote best practices and knowledge exchange between municipalities in climate and energy related issues. With IRH support, the project will support collaboration of the target municipalities with their regional, Danish, and other EU member states counterparts for enhanced learning and implementation of successful solutions in Georgian municipalities. The project will support participation of municipalities in the regional knowledge-share platforms and events, study tours. With IRH support, the project will explore opportunities and provide technical support to municipalities for mobilizing additional funds through partnerships with EU-member states municipalities (e.g., Constanta (Romania), Varna (Bulgaria) - sister cities of Poti), other state and donors’ funding opportunities to support sustainability of changes. The project will provide funding to the municipalities for implementing selected municipal initiatives to support introduction of the explored best practices and solutions, as well as effective implementation of the projects with the additionally mobilized funds. The technical assistance, capacity building and cooperation enhancement components to advance green and just economic transformations and local governance in Georgia, use of digital tools and technologies in public governance, improvement of communication on the benefits of green and just transition, as well as project impact, will be backed by IRH support under activities of sub-outputs 3.1. and 3.2.

description.narrative: Energy efficiency and green transition-related courses and upskilling opportunities will be offered to vulnerable groups (rural youth, women, IDPs, and PwDs), equipping them with the skills and knowledge required for existing and new green jobs. Since energy auditors can work as individual entrepreneurs and MoESD publishes the list of certified auditors, they will have good prospects of generating income without being employed by private businesses . Therefore, the project will support certification processes, assisting candidates, particularly IDPs, women, and youth, in accessing training, preparing for certification exams, and understanding the legal and regulatory requirements for practicing as energy auditors or related professionals. Addressing gender-based barriers, the project will explore opportunities for women's inclusion in green transition jobs through targeted training, mentorship, and networking initiatives. Support will be provided to women entrepreneurs and innovators to access green job sectors, leverage their skills, and overcome knowledge gaps to thrive in green economy roles. The project will partner with other projects focused on women’s economic empowerment.

description.narrative: Energy efficiency legislation now requires municipalities, state property owners, and large businesses to implement energy efficiency audits conducted by certified energy auditors. Starting from December 2023, energy efficiency audits will be mandatory for issuing building permits. However, the list of certified energy auditors published by MoESD on its website includes only eighteen auditors, insufficient to meet the demand defined by the law. The legislation also mandates energy efficiency labeling for all buildings, including the provision of an energy efficiency passport when renting or selling residential apartments. The law specifies the following regulated qualifications: a) Energy audit implementers in the industry sector; b) Energy auditors implementing energy efficiency certification of buildings; c) Energy managers and installers of elements affecting energy consumption by buildings; d) Independent experts performing inspections of heating and air conditioning systems in buildings; e) Persons performing energy audits in the buildings sector. Similar requirements are outlined by other laws concerning photovoltaic (solar panels) service personnel and environmental managers. Although national standards for relevant professional education qualifications have been established, educational programs are not yet developed. The project will support public Vocational Education College "Phazisi" and Zugdidi University, to develop professional education training and retraining programs, which will serve as a replicable model for other areas in the country, introduce relevant professional education and skills development programs in these educational institutions aligned with market needs and support delivery of skills development programs. The project will partner with Energy Efficiency Center in development, introduction, implementation and certfification of energy efficiency related qualificiations, including in providing support to Phazisi College and Zugdidi University. . . The project will collaborate with Sector Skills Organizations and private sector associations, to enhance and stimulate demand for green jobs from the private sector. This collaboration will build links between professional colleges and the private sector to increase the employability of reskilled and upskilled personnel. Facilitating internships to bridge the gap between education and employment and advocating for the hiring of certified professionals are also key components. Participants will receive career counseling and job placement support to secure employment in energy efficiency-related jobs after completing their training.

title.narrative: Number of Area Development Plans elaborated with the participation of local communities

description.narrative: The Khobi and Poti municipalities have strong interlinked dynamics, making them a strategic focus for the GFP interventions. Research conducted during the inception period has validated the connections between Khobi and Poti across various intervention areas, with clear ties to the wider region, and particularly with the Zugdidi municipality. About 7,000 Khobi residents commute daily to Poti and Zugdidi for work, business, or education, while Khobi serves as an agricultural supply base for these cities. The municipalities, located along the Black Sea shore and within the same river basins, are naturally linked in addressing common environmental and climate issues. Additionally, the regional landfill system connects all nine municipalities, with waste management centralized at the Zugdidi regional landfill. Building on these connections, and after close consultations with the Greening the Future Project Team, the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure (MRDI) in Georgia has agreed to include the Poti and Khobi municipalities in the new the new Integrated Territorial Development Program (ITDP), alongside Zugdidi. Supported by an additional 50 million EUR from the EU, the new ITDP will fund area-based solutions and policy documents after government approval – enabling this way scalability and a wider reaching impact for the GFP. MRDI has introduced ITDPs with the Regional Development Programming in 2018-2021, shifting from infrastructure-focused model of local-level development to integrated territorial actions aligned with EU standards. After the pilot program's success in four regions, MRDI is expanding these principles to other areas. Consequently, the project will develop joint area-based development document for Poti and Khobi municipalities to explore Poti functional urban area, uncover functional linkages with neighboring municipalities, opportunities, common challenges and area-based solutions outcoming from the existing funcitional linkages between these municipalities. The research will suggest area-based solutions to promote green and just transition in the defined functional area, which will be incorporated in the project interventions. The document development process will leverage UNDP's prior work via the DGG Project, which introduced and institutionalized participatory methodologies for municipal development planning and created Municipal Development Documents (MDDs) for Poti and Khobi municipalities, among others. Consequently, the MDDs, local economic development plan, SDG localization plans and other strategic local development documents of Poti and Khobi municipalities will serve as a foundation for the project activities, aimed inter alia at addressing underprivileged areas and communities. Workshops and consultations with local communities, the private sector, and national and local actors will align governance strategies with these priorities, enhancing social cohesion and stability. Knowledge products, policy, and technical support from IRH under sub-output 3.1 will be analyzed and applied in creating the area-based development document.

title.narrative: Number of employees of private and public institutions that have improved green transition related skills

description.narrative: The project will also provide specialized training and upskilling opportunities to job-seekers and existing employees of private and public institutions, equipping them with the knowledge and skills required for energy efficiency, renewable energy, waste management, eco-tourism, sustainable agriculture and other green jobs. Training courses will be based on skills gap assessments and incorporate hands-on, practical training components whenever possible, enabling employees to apply their learning directly to their work tasks. Additionally, the project will provide training to local companies’ owners to promote and implement energy efficiency, sustainable green practices principles within their organizations, with a comprehensive coaching curriculum led by subject matter experts and industry leaders. This strategic approach ensures that the knowledge and skills acquired through the training directly contribute to improved job performance and, consequently, to the overall efficiency and sustainability of the institutions involved.

title.narrative: Number of initiatives, projects and improvements to support green transition developed and initiatied with project support.

description.narrative: The project will also support municipalities in adhering to energy efficiency, renewable energy, waste management legislation and NECP requirements. For instance, municipalities must develop energy consumption passports for all municipal buildings, ensure energy efficiency measures in 1% of municipal properties (increasing to 3), and issue building permits for all buildings up to 50m² based on an energy efficiency audit by a certified auditor, in line with new EU building regulations. The project will bolster enhance these activities by raising awareness, building the capacity of relevant municipal staff, and developing energy management systems, energy efficiency consulting services, and support municipalities in promoting energy efficiency measures, increased use of solar energy systems in municipal operations, local communities and private sector. Further, the project will assist municipalities and local stakeholders in implementing approved Waste Management Plans, including waste separation, and provide technical assistance for planning waste management operations, particularly waste separation, construction waste management, billing database development, waste-related data collection, and public awareness initiatives. New waste management concepts like waste reuse (including green waste), prevention, reduction and efficient management of food waste, packaging waste will also be supported, along with facilitating dialogue and supporting private sector in implementation of extended producers responsibilities in cooperation with the producers’ responsibility organizations for prevention, reduction, sustainable management and recycling of private sector waste, promoting reuse and recycling of separated waste, including single-use plastics— a prevalent issue in both municipalities along their river basins and Black Sea shoreline. Coupled with MRDI and other donor engagements, the project assistance in waste management will enhance project impact and promote the sustainable use of green practices, fostering systemic cooperation between the target municipalities. The project will also support municipalities in development of public transportation. Poti will benefit from support in developing a parking concept, a smart traffic light system and other actions to manage heavy transit cargo traffic from the port through the city, the digitalization of public transport, and other measures aimed for improved public transportation system. Khobi municipality, lacking its own public transportation, will require support for a needs analysis, considering daily commuting within adjacent rural communities and between Zugdidi and Poti municipalities. A parking concept for Khobi will also be supported, as well as development of sustainable urban transport plans for the municipalities. Like waste management, while the project will not fund the purchase of public transportation, it will provide technical support to enable municipalities to implement necessary actions to develop public transport systems, digitalization, optimization, greening and improvement of existing public transport operations with their own, state, and donor funds. The project will educate municipal staff on green infrastructure investments, such as green roofs, urban parks, and sustainable drainage systems, and support the development of sustainable urban planning practices, green space policies, standards for efficient energy and water use, plants selection, application of nature-based solutions, and the adaptation of green spaces for women, children, PwD, and the elderly. Additionally, there is a need to develop new green and blue corridors for climate adaptation and support both municipalities in planning and implementation of climate adaptation, disaster prevention and emergency response policies and measures.

title.narrative: Number of improved energy efficiency, waste management, transportation and green transition related practices

description.narrative: The project will also support municipalities in development of public transportation. Poti will benefit from support in developing a parking concept, a smart traffic light system and other actions to manage heavy transit cargo traffic from the port through the city, the digitalization of public transport, and other measures aimed for improved public transportation system. Khobi municipality, lacking its own public transportation, will require support for a needs analysis, considering daily commuting within adjacent rural communities and between Zugdidi and Poti municipalities. A parking concept for Khobi will also be supported, as well as development of sustainable urban transport plans for the municipalities. Like waste management, while the project will not fund the purchase of public transportation, it will provide technical support to enable municipalities to implement necessary actions to develop public transport systems, digitalization, optimization, greening and improvement of existing public transport operations with their own, state, and donor funds. The project will educate municipal staff on green infrastructure investments, such as green roofs, urban parks, and sustainable drainage systems, and support the development of sustainable urban planning practices, green space policies, standards for efficient energy and water use, plants selection, application of nature-based solutions, and the adaptation of green spaces for women, children, PwD, and the elderly. Additionally, there is a need to develop new green and blue corridors for climate adaptation and support both municipalities in planning and implementation of climate adaptation, disaster prevention and emergency response policies and measures. As previously mentioned, the UNESCO-protected Kolkheti National Park spans both municipalities. Despite both municipalities prioritizing tourism in their MDDs, neither currently benefits significantly from tourist activities. Leveraging the region's cultural and natural heritage, the project will aid municipalities in planning and developing eco-tourism initiatives for sustainable tourism while preserving biodiversity and cultural identity. Both municipalities will receive support for developing relevant branding, conducting feasibility studies, and conceptualizing access and a visitor center for the National Park in Khobi municipality, in collaboration with the State Protected Areas Agency and Tourism Administration. The project will cooperate with APM Terminals Poti Port, being part of Maersk Transport and Logistics, to share and apply Danish private sector experience in waste management and efficient energy management with municipalities and private sector stakeholders, and support uptake of sustainable practices by the local stakeholders. The development of area-based analyses of neighbouring municipalities, described in action 1.1.1, along with the development of Khobi municipality's SECAP and the monitoring and review of Poti's SECAP, will provide additional information essential for designing project interventions for the green and just transition.

Municipal authorities will receive technical support in designing, integrating, and executing local programs, including elaboration and mid-term reviews of SECAPs, area-based development, eco-tourism development, including unlocking potential of Kolkheti National Park related tourism and local economic development, sustainable and eco smart urban development and transformation, climate adaptation, disaster prevention and emergency response, and other municipal green and just transition related policy documents and action plans.

title.narrative: Number of citizen participation initiatives, awareness raising campaigns and projects implemented by CSOs.

description.narrative: The project will empower CSOs, business association, producers responsibility organizations with small grants to support community-led projects that promote green and just transition, climate and energy agenda, green growth and social accountability. It will, facilitate participatory planning processes and consultations with communities through CSOs, engage local residents, including women, youth, IDPs, and marginalized groups, private sector in decision-making and implementation processes related to municipal planning, environmental policies, climate adaptation, green infrastructure development, green and just transition, green growth and social accountability. Additionally, the project will support advocacy, awareness raising and behavioral changes campaigns to educate the public and private sector about green transition goals, environmental rights, and the benefits of sustainable practices. To increase motivation of both governmental and non-governmental actors to work together and leverage grants provided to CSOs, the project will also provide support and funding to the municipalities for strengthening citizen engagement activities from the municipalities side, such as support design, implementing and co-funding participatory budgeting programs, youth programs and activities, functioning of municipalities existing participatory platforms (mayors advisory, youth, gender, PwD councils), Youth Center established by Poti municipality, and support of their programs and activities, organizing meetings, focus groups, surveys, creating visibility and learning materials, support in public communicating of the policy development, dual transition and implementation of area-based and green transition related plans, as well as public awareness campaigns supporting green and just transition, behavioral changes in local communities and private sector. The project will partner with the municipalities to channel support schemes, innovation challenges and other target programs aimed at increased engagement of local community groups represented by mayors advisory, youth, gender, PwD councils.

title.narrative: Number of municipal programing documents, investment portfolios, action plans aimed to support green transition and area based development designed by the project support

description.narrative: The project will offer technical assistance to local institutions, with a two-fold focus: a) updating and implementing municipal programs in response to area-based priorities, and b) promoting partnerships with the local private sector to advance green transition. Targeted municipal authorities will receive support in designing, integrating, and executing local programs addressing green and just transition, human rights, gender equality, youth empowerment, energy efficiency, ecological challenges and potential, and other relevant priorities within their competencies. . Within the scope of the decentralization reform and with the support of the DGG project, municipalities' access to grants from international organizations was simplified, allowing them to initiate and manage local development initiatives through donor support. Therefore, the project will provide funding for implementing selected municipal initiatives based on the above programs to address major challenges and unlock local development prospects, with a focus on climate, energy, adequate preservation of unique nature and sustainable realization of ecological potential. Additionally, the project will facilitate partnership-building between local governments and private sector actors exploring the potential for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and encouraging the sharing of knowledge, best practices, and technology.

title.narrative: Number of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) provided with capacity development support. Sub-targets for CSOs led by women and/or youth OR working on empowering women and/or youth

description.narrative: The project will strengthen the capacities of the local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)/ Community-based Organizations (CBOs), business associations, producers responsibility organizations working in Khobi and Poti municipalities through trainings and workshops in the most needed areas to increase knowledge and skills that will contribute to meaningful participation in policy dialogue, advocacy, project design, and management, including resource mobilization (e.g., advocacy, project design, storytelling, social accountability, identification of community needs, citizen engagement mechanisms, resource mobilization, etc.), dual transition and local development. CSOs working in the targeted areas/municipalities will be also offered an opportunity to engage in various forms of collaboration, and form alliances and partnerships to amplify their impact. These collaborations aim to enhance their advocacy efforts and allow for resource sharing. The project will focus on and mainstream green transition issues in the CSOs and in general citizen engagement. For example, strengthening of CSOs capacities will include awareness-raising on just, green, and digital transition, mentorship programs, and technical assistance to empower local organizations in advocating for and implementing green initiatives, as well as to function as drivers of green transition in the local communities and private sector. Green awards, development of digital participatory and monitoring tools and other mechanisms will be applied to increase motivation of CSOs and communities they serve to participate in the green transition. The project will provide need based technical assistance to CSOs, business associations, producers responsibility organizations in monitoring and evaluating the impact of their initiatives on green transition outcomes, develop monitoring frameworks, data collection tools, and evaluation methodologies to assess project effectiveness and inform evidence-based decision-making. Small grants for research, independent data collection, review and monitoring of municipal policies and activities, citizen satisfaction reviews and similar activities will be financed to promote CSOs engagement and learning by doing. IRH Regional knowledge-sharing platform on green transition, Danish participatory practices, courses like Just and Green Transition developed by UNDP Urban Learning Center, other UNDP resources, will be applied where possible. IRH digital, AI related components, including for countering disinformation in green transition will be addressed. Like in municipalities, knowledge sharing and CSOs capacity-building to mobilize funding for green transition related initiatives will be supported.

title.narrative: Green transition related data collection and monitoring mechanism established in targeted two municipalities

description.narrative: The project will support local institutions to establish and administer continued data collection and monitoring tools to track the effectiveness and accountability of local governance improvements. However, for the bigger impact the project will concentrate on the data related to green transition, such as data for development and monitoring SECAPs, waste management plans, urban mobility plans and similar data in project related activities. For better understanding and addressing gender disparities, inequalities, and barriers in green sectors, the project will support gender-responsive data collection and monitoring tools. The same approach will be used to ensure data collection and monitoring for understanding and addressing the social aspects of green transition on disadvantaged groups, including IDPs, PwD, the elderly and other socially vulnerable communities, to equip the municipalities with data and knowledge to ensure not only green, but also a just transition. In cooperation with MRDI, Geostat, the project will identify relevant data set, elaborate methodology and digital tools as necessary for data collection and will support municipalitiesy and Geostat with capacity building and technical assistance, including with support of IRH for use of bigdata and AI data monitoring tools (activity 3.2.2)

title.narrative: d) Number of municipal staff trained in green and just transition regulatory frameworks, effective planning and implementation and related mobilization of finance

description.narrative: The project will support targeted capacity-building for local government officials on environmental governance, climate action planning, and sustainable development strategies. This includes incorporating green transition issues and behavioral changes in budgeting, introduction of green budgeting, procurement, infrastructure and urban planning, municipal services, municipality-to-business relations, social services, community engagement, policy-development and improving public communication on green and just transition, including counterfeiting disinformation and misperceptions. In addition to strengthening local planning capabilities, based on the lessons learned through the DGG project, GFP will support the target municipalities in donor relations capacity-building. This will be achieved through technical assistance and capacity building for accessing funding sources and grants specifically earmarked for green initiatives. It will also include development of grant applications to obtain direct grants from MRDI and other ministries, donors, EU funds and improve capacity of the target municipalities to manage grants on a learning by doing basis.

For achieving sustainable and inclusive development outcomes, the project will specifically target policies and investments, supporting gender empowerment and inclusion in green transition, based on the research on gender gaps and opportunities for promoting women inclusion.

title.narrative: Labour market baseline report

description.narrative: The report “Penetration of EE and RE Technologies in Georgian SMEs” and an online survey of local businesses conducted during the inception period identify a lack of awareness, knowledge, and skilled personnel as major barriers to energy efficiency and green transition. A relevant labour market and skills development mapping report, will be prepared to assess the need to address these skill deficiencies to promote green transition, particularly energy efficiency.

In its capacity development activities, the project will utilize the learning and managerial tools already developed by UNDP including public service development guidebooks prepared and PMS for waste management and street cleaning, and other learning materials.

title.narrative: Number of local municipal staff with increased capacities in people-centered service delivery

description.narrative: To create an enabling environment for re/designing municipal services, the project will address capacity gaps related to planning, designing, delivering, and evaluating municipal services. A series of tailored training sessions and on-the-job mentorship support will be extended to municipal staff members. This intervention will place significant emphasis on raising awareness among participants and enhancing their competencies in delivering people-centered services, as well as ensuring that key services are delivered in a rights-based and inclusive manner.

title.narrative: Number of Digital Ambassadors supported to increase access to e-services

description.narrative: To support service delivery in remote and disadvantaged areas of Khobi municipality, the project will support e-service delivery through the enhancement of service delivery by offices of Mayors' representatives in Khobi municipality administrative units. The offices of Mayors’ representatives can provide support to local communities to access municipal services digitally through the unified e-services platform, which provides opportunity to citizens to address local authorities and access services remotely. Public uptake of the platform remains low as for a citizen to be able to use all available services, along with personal computer connected to internet, one should have electronic ID, pin code, digital signature, and ID card reader. Considering the lack of access to these devices and lack of digital literacy among most vulnerable population, the mayors’ offices in administrative units can serve as a connecting point providing necessary support to citizens to access the basic services remotely without traveling to the administrative center. With the objective to increase the access to e-services offered by the offices of Mayors' representatives the project will supply essential technical equipment to their offices and provide training and consultancy to Mayor’s representatives to fully utilize opportunities created via unified e-services platform. In addition to advancing Mayor’s representatives capacities, to address the root causes of the problem such as lack of digital literacy of the population or lack of digital readers both in Khobi and Poti municipalities, the project will support local activists and community groups, women, girls, youth in rural communities and in IDP settlements to educate and empower them with the knowledge and digital readers to assist their neighbors in using available e-services, participation in decision making and increased accountability of the municipalities. Such activities will be also in the focus of CSOs under sub-output 1.3. The project will also support digitalization of other existing municipal services, development of web and mobile applications in both municipalities, digitalization of public transportation in Poti municipality and other. . In this regard the project will also partner with Georgia Innovation and Technology Agency (GITA), Municipal Service Development Agency (MSDA) and Service Development Agency (SDA). IRH support and knowledge base on digital and AI solutions in e-solutions will be actively utilized.

title.narrative: Number of national and regional initiatives (studies, technical assistance, workshops, donor coordination meetings) supported for increased policy dialogue and role of the municipalities

description.narrative: UNDP will engage with the central government to local and regional development actors to enhance coordination and cooperation, stimulating green transition and green growth. The project will ensure multi-level coordination that will foster green and just transition on local level that is sustainable beyond the life of the project. UNDP will assist the central and local governments towards continued policy dialogue, support development of national and regional strategic documents with a focus on climate and energy, green and just transition, increased roles and resources of municipalities in deciding affairs of local importance, by conducting relevant studies, providing expert support, and organizing discussions between central and local authorities. This will also help to ensure that area-based and municipalities needs and priorities are aligned with and reflected in national priorities. To ensure the mainstreaming of the green, just, and digital transition agenda in regional development policy, priorities and activities of other municipalities and other donors' engagements, the project will support MRDI in establishing and operationalizing the Donor Coordination Platform on Regional Development, similar to the donor coordination platform coordinated by MRDI in the decentralization area with UNDP office support (formerly under DGG and currently under EU4ITD projects). The project will support the mapping of the relevant donors, funding donor coordination meetings and elaboration of the data-base tools, which will serve as an information sharing platform for governments and donors in the engagements in the The project will work and support NALAG in strengthening its capacities to promote dialogue on climate and energy issues between national and subnational governance. Support will be provided to strengthen capacities of the Coordination Council comprised of the municipalities - signatories of the Covenant of Mayor and acting as subnational level consultative body under National Climate Council.
